pr.title: Remove the test suite's temporary files when a run exits
pr.head: 3b1c53658e24701a15c096c5ccb420d859e6d991

summary: Projector's test suite builds scratch Git repositories, site builds, and summary files in the system temporary directory, using tempfile.mkdtemp. About 45 of those calls never remove what they create, so one full run leaves 336 directories, about 19,000 inodes, behind. A review loop runs the suite at every head it reviews. On a machine whose /tmp is a tmpfs with a fixed number of inodes, several loops running in parallel fill it within hours, and every program that writes there then fails with No space left on device.

This change fixes the leak in one place instead of at each call. tests/__init__.py, which Python imports before any test module, creates one projector-tests-* directory per run and makes it the temporary directory for the run and for every subprocess the run starts. When the run exits, an atexit handler deletes that directory and everything in it.

The review of this head found no problems. The full suite passes and leaves its temporary directory empty, both on a normal exit and after SIGINT. A run killed with SIGKILL skips atexit handlers and still leaves its one directory behind.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• tempfile.tempdir: the module-level setting that Python's tempfile functions use as their parent directory when it is set.
  • TMPDIR: the environment variable that Python, Git, and most Unix programs read to choose a temporary directory. Child processes inherit it.
  • atexit: the Python module that runs registered functions when the interpreter exits normally, including after an unhandled exception such as KeyboardInterrupt, but not after SIGKILL.

groups.title: One temporary directory per test run
groups.kicker: The test package's setup creates a per-run temporary directory and deletes it at exit.
intro: The tests package's __init__.py already prepares the environment for every test, for example by clearing the GITHUB_REPOSITORY variable that GitHub Actions sets. It now also creates a fresh directory under the caller's temporary directory, and points both tempfile.tempdir and TMPDIR at it.

Setting tempfile.tempdir moves every mkdtemp and TemporaryDirectory call in the test process under the new directory. Setting TMPDIR does the same for the subprocesses the tests start, such as git and project. One atexit handler then removes the whole tree, so a test added later that forgets to clean up leaks nothing either.

files.note: Creates the per-run directory, redirects temporary files into it, and registers its removal at exit.

checks.text: The directory is created under whatever temporary directory the caller chose, because the first mkdtemp call reads TMPDIR before this file changes it. Running the suite with TMPDIR set to an empty directory left that directory empty afterwards, after 454 tests passed.

Nothing under src/ reads TMPDIR or tempfile.gettempdir, so the redirect changes where files go, not what the code does. The one test that sets its own TMPDIR, the site serve signal test in tests/test_site.py, passes a directory that now sits inside the run's directory.

The handler also runs when you interrupt the suite: sending SIGINT six seconds into a run left the temporary directory empty. The suite uses neither os.fork nor multiprocessing, so no child process inherits this handler and deletes the directory while the parent is still running.

This setup runs only when the test modules are imported as part of the tests package, as python3 -m unittest discover from the repository root does in CI and in the documented gate. Running discover -s tests or a test file directly skips it, along with the existing environment resets in the same file.
